sentences.text: Subrata Mandal & Anr vs Unknown on 4 October, 2024

Author: Soumen Sen Bench: Soumen Sen  04.10.2024  SL No.12  Court No.29  (gc)
 (Allowed)
 CRM (A) 2889 of 2024  In Re:- An application for anticipatory bail under Sec  Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 corresponding to Sect  the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in connec  Santipur Police Station Case No. 895 of 2024 dated 01.
 under Sections 448/376/511/506/34 of the Indian Penal   corresponding to Sections 329(4)/64/62/351/3(5) of the  And  In the matter of : Subrata Mandal & Anr.
 
 Mr. Susnigdho Bhattacharyya  ....For the Petitioners.
 Ms. Minoti Gomes,
 Ms. Ankita Paul  ... For the State.
Mr. Z. Islam  ....For the De facto Complainant.

1. 
The victim was the aunt of the petitioner no.1.
She was married to the uncle of the petitioner no.1 and after divorce she remarried.
The petitioner no.2 is the friend of the petitioner no.1.
It is submitted that due to family dispute, the petitioners have been falsely implicated.
2. The learned Counsel for the State and the de facto complainant have opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

3. Ms. Minoti Gomes, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the State has referred to the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and the statement of the husband recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text:
4. Considering the materials available in the case diary, the nature and extent of complicity of the petitioners in the commission of the Signed By :
GURUPADA CHAKRABARTY High Court of Calcutta 4 th of October 2024 05:11:50 PM alleged offence and having regard to the fact that the petitioner no.2 is not being named either by the de facto complainant or by the husband of the de facto complainant and also having regard to the nature of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in relation to the petitioner no.1, we are of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioners is not necessary.

5. Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest, the petitioners namely, Subrata Mandal and Rahul Biswas @ Raju, shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- each, with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the arresting officer and also subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C., 1973 corresponding to Section 482(2) of the BNSS, 2023 and on further condition that the petitioners shall meet the I.O. once in a fortnight till the submission of the final report.

6. It is further directed that the petitioners shall appear before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Ranaghat, Nadia in connection with G.R. Case No.2872 of 2024 on or before 8th October, 2024.

8. All parties shall act on the server copy of this order duly downloaded from the official website of this Court.
